title: Boss: the token service
summary: Issue tokens, validate them against a key ring without falling for algorithm confusion, and rotate refresh tokens with reuse detection.

steps.title: The token service
body: You are writing the token layer for a company with an identity server and several APIs:
1. **Issue** HS256 access tokens with all the right claims.
2. **Validate** tokens against a *key ring*: several keys, each bound to one algorithm, selected by `kid`. This is how real validators defeat algorithm confusion.
3. **Refresh** with rotation, hashing and reuse detection.
All times are passed in. No clock reads.

steps.title: Issue access tokens
prompt: Write a class `JwtIssuer`:
- `JwtIssuer(byte[] secret, string issuer, string audience, TimeSpan lifetime)`: throw `ArgumentException` if the secret is shorter than 32 bytes.

- `string Issue(string subject, string[] roles, long now, string jti)`: an HS256 token with header `{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}` and claims `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `iat` = `now`, `nbf` = `now`, `exp` = `now + lifetime` in seconds, `jti`, and `roles` as a JSON array.

Build the payload with `JsonSerializer.Serialize` (of a `Dictionary<string, object>` or an anonymous object). The tests decode your token and check each claim and the signature. They import `System.Security.Cryptography` and `System.Text.Json`.
starter: public JwtIssuer(byte[] secret, string issuer, string audience, TimeSpan lifetime) { }
public string Issue(string subject, string[] roles, long now, string jti) => "";
solution: public JwtIssuer(byte[] secret, string issuer, string audience, TimeSpan lifetime)
if (secret.Length < 32) throw new ArgumentException("HS256 secrets must be at least 32 bytes.");
public string Issue(string subject, string[] roles, long now, string jti)
private static string B64(string text) => B64(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(text));
hints: Validate the secret length in the constructor and store the four settings.
`JsonSerializer.Serialize(new Dictionary<string, object> { ["iss"] = ..., ["roles"] = roles })` produces the payload JSON.
Private static helpers inside the class can do base64url.
template: Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a 16-byte secret is refused", () => new JwtIssuer(new byte[16], "i", "a", TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)));
Dojo.Eq("the signature is HMAC-SHA256 with the secret", dojoResigned.Split('.')[2], dojoParts[2]);
string Claim(string n) => dojoP.TryGetProperty(n, out var v) ? v.ToString() : "(missing)";

Dojo.Eq("roles is an array", "user,editor", dojoP.TryGetProperty("roles", out var dojoR) && dojoR.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join(",", dojoR.EnumerateArray().Select(x => x.GetString())) : "(not an array)");
public static string Hs(string header, string payload, byte[] secret)
public static string Hs(string payload, byte[] secret) => Hs(Hs256Header, payload, secret);
public static string Es(string header, string payload, System.Security.Cryptography.ECDsa key)

steps.title: A key ring validator
prompt: Write `string Validate(string token, Dictionary<string, JwtKey> keys, string issuer, string audience, long now)`.
The tests define `record JwtKey(string Alg, byte[]? Secret, ECDsa? PublicKey);`. Each key is bound to **one** algorithm: an `"HS256"` key has a `Secret`, an `"ES256"` key has a `PublicKey`.
Return the first problem, in this order:
| Return | When |
| `"malformed"` | not three parts, undecodable, or not JSON |
| `"unknown_key"` | no string `kid` in the header, or it isn't in `keys` |
| `"bad_alg"` | the header's `alg` differs from **the key's** `Alg` |
| `"bad_signature"` | the signature fails for that key's algorithm |
| `"malformed"` | no numeric `exp` in the payload |
| `"expired"` | `now >= exp + 30` |
| `"bad_issuer"` / `"bad_audience"` | as before (`aud` may be an array) |
The payload's claims are only read once the signature is good, so a tampered token is `"bad_signature"` even if its payload has no `exp`. Never throw.
The algorithm comes from the key, never from the token, so an attacker who signs an HS256 token using the ES256 key's public bytes gets `bad_alg`.
Bring your own `B64Url` / `FromB64Url`. The tests import `System.Security.Cryptography` and `System.Text.Json`.
starter: string Validate(string token, Dictionary<string, JwtKey> keys, string issuer, string audience, long now)
solution: case 1: throw new FormatException("Not valid base64url.");
string Validate(string token, Dictionary<string, JwtKey> keys, string issuer, string audience, long now)
if (!h.TryGetProperty("kid", out var kid) || kid.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String) return "unknown_key";
if (!h.TryGetProperty("alg", out var alg) || alg.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String || alg.GetString() != key.Alg) return "bad_alg";
"HS256" => key.Secret is not null && CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(HMACSHA256.HashData(key.Secret, input), sig),
"ES256" => key.PublicKey is not null && key.PublicKey.VerifyData(input, sig, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256),
if (!root.TryGetProperty("exp", out var exp) || exp.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Number) return "malformed";
if (!root.TryGetProperty("iss", out var iss) || iss.GetString() != issuer) return "bad_issuer";
JsonValueKind.Array => aud.EnumerateArray().Any(a => a.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.String && a.GetString() == audience),
catch (Exception e) when (e is FormatException or JsonException or InvalidOperationException)
hints: Look up the key by `kid` first; then compare `alg` with `key.Alg`.
`switch` on `key.Alg` to pick HMAC with `FixedTimeEquals` or `PublicKey.VerifyData`.
The claim checks are the same as in the validation lesson, with a 30-second skew.
template: Dojo.Eq("HS256 token with kid hs-1", "ok", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("ES256 token with kid ec-1", "ok", Validate(DojoJwt.Es("{\"alg\":\"ES256\",\"kid\":\"ec-1\"}", Body, dojoEc), dojoKeys, Iss, "files-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("no kid -> unknown_key", "unknown_key", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("unknown kid -> unknown_key", "unknown_key", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-9\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));

Dojo.Eq("algorithm confusion: HS256 'signed' with the EC public key, kid ec-1 -> bad_alg", "bad_alg", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"ec-1\"}", Body, dojoPubBytes), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("alg none with a real kid -> bad_alg", "bad_alg", Validate(DojoJwt.B64("{\"alg\":\"none\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}") + "." + DojoJwt.B64(Body) + ".", dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("HS256 with the wrong secret -> bad_signature", "bad_signature", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}", Body, new byte[32]), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("tampered ES256 -> bad_signature", "bad_signature", Validate(DojoJwt.Tamper(DojoJwt.Es("{\"alg\":\"ES256\",\"kid\":\"ec-1\"}", Body, dojoEc)), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("expired (exp + 30 reached) -> expired", "expired", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 2030));
Dojo.Eq("inside skew -> ok", "ok", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, Iss, "tasks-api", 2029));
Dojo.Eq("wrong issuer -> bad_issuer", "bad_issuer", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, "https://other", "tasks-api", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("not in the audience -> bad_audience", "bad_audience", Validate(DojoJwt.Hs("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"kid\":\"hs-1\"}", Body, dojoHs), dojoKeys, Iss, "billing-api", 1000));
record JwtKey(string Alg, byte[]? Secret, ECDsa? PublicKey);
public static string Hs(string header, string payload, byte[] secret)
public static string Hs(string payload, byte[] secret) => Hs(Hs256Header, payload, secret);
public static string Es(string header, string payload, System.Security.Cryptography.ECDsa key)

steps.title: Refresh tokens with rotation and reuse detection
prompt: Write a class `RefreshTokenStore`:
- `RefreshTokenStore(TimeSpan lifetime)`
- `string Issue(string user, DateTimeOffset now)`: a new random token (at least 32 random bytes, as hex) that starts a new **family**.
- `(string Token, string User)? Rotate(string token, DateTimeOffset now)`:
- unknown token, expired token (`now >= issued + lifetime`), or a token whose family is revoked -> `null`
- a token that was **already rotated** -> revoke its whole family and return `null`
- otherwise mark it used and return a new token **in the same family**, plus the user.
- `void RevokeAll(string user)`: revoke every family of that user (logout everywhere).
- `bool StoresRawToken(string token)`: return `true` if your storage contains the token text itself as a key. The tests expect `false`: store `SHA256` hashes of tokens, not the tokens.
The tests import `System.Security.Cryptography`.
starter: public string Issue(string user, DateTimeOffset now) => "";
public (string Token, string User)? Rotate(string token, DateTimeOffset now) => null;
solution: public string Issue(string user, DateTimeOffset now) => New(user, Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N"), now);
public (string Token, string User)? Rotate(string token, DateTimeOffset now)
if (!_byHash.TryGetValue(Hash(token), out var e)) return null;
private string New(string user, string family, DateTimeOffset now)
_byHash[Hash(token)] = new Entry { User = user, Family = family, Expires = now + _lifetime };
hints: Give each entry a `Family` id (a new GUID per `Issue`) and a `Used` flag; keep a `HashSet<string>` of revoked families.
In `Rotate`: unknown -> null; revoked family -> null; used -> revoke family, null; expired -> null; else mark used and create a new entry with the same family.
template: Dojo.Check("tokens are at least 64 characters", dojoR1.Length >= 64, dojoR1);
Dojo.Eq("the raw token is not stored", false, dojoS.StoresRawToken(dojoR1));
Dojo.Check("rotating a fresh token works", dojoStep is not null, "got null");
Dojo.Check("the new token differs", dojoR2 != dojoR1, dojoR2);
Dojo.Check("the new token rotates too", dojoStep3 is not null, "got null");
Dojo.Eq("replaying the first token -> null", null, dojoS.Rotate(dojoR1, dojoT0.AddHours(3)));
Dojo.Eq("...and the whole family is revoked: the newest token fails", null, dojoS.Rotate(dojoR3, dojoT0.AddHours(3)));
Dojo.Eq("another family is unaffected", "grace", dojoS.Rotate(dojoG, dojoT0.AddHours(3))?.User);
Dojo.Eq("a token at its lifetime -> null", null, dojoS.Rotate(dojoOld, dojoT0.AddDays(14)));
Dojo.Eq("an unknown token -> null", null, dojoS.Rotate("deadbeef", dojoT0));
Dojo.Eq("RevokeAll kills carol's first login", null, dojoS.Rotate(dojoA1, dojoT0.AddHours(1)));
Dojo.Eq("and her second", null, dojoS.Rotate(dojoA2, dojoT0.AddHours(1)));
